criteria.rationale: Examined the assumptions. Verified: no caller of VerifyReviewRunProofForReading uses its result to back a new attestation (three callers only print or fill Issuer metadata; conclude/adjudication/smoke/fulfilment stay on VerifyReviewRunProof at review_conclusions.go:568, delegated_verdicts.go:428, delegated_review_request.go:300); an unreadable bundle falls back to the live verifier, which fails closed. Unresolved but stated: the adjudication/smoke gap (spec Known gaps). Accepted risk: low follow-ups F2-F4.

The new function is a read-only dispatcher with no shared state, locks or goroutines. A scope that turns done between the dispatch check and the verification only changes which read-only question is answered; no write depends on it.

The output shape of the 'pose review run-proof' CLI is unchanged (same ReviewRunAssurance rendering). Its meaning for done scopes changes on purpose and is disclosed in the changelog (category fixed) and the manual. The new exported Go function is additive.

Errors from LoadProvenanceReviewRun, runProofPath and the verifiers propagate unchanged; when the bundle cannot be read or lifecycle detection fails, the function falls back to the live verifier, which is fail-closed (review_run_provenance.go:674-677).
The CLI, delegated verdict and conclusion-recovery consumers now share the closeout's dispatch (runApprovalAsSealed). Retained-approval and conclusion integration checks remain sealed as passing.
Failures still return the verifier's bounded 'run provenance: ...' reasons; no new logging, and no secrets are exposed.

Examined the CLI and MCP surfaces: no flag, file format or tool schema changed; open scopes keep the live answer (TestTheProofReaderKeepsTheLiveQuestionForAnOpenScope). The more permissive reading for done scopes is documented in the manual (EN/pt-BR, root and scaffold) and in the changelog.

The done-scope test shows the closeout approves, the live verifier refuses and the reader agrees with the closeout; the open-scope test shows the reader refuses after drift. Together they rule out an always-live or always-sealed reader.

Cause: the readers called VerifyReviewRunProof while the closeout used runApprovalAsSealed to choose between sealed and live. Design: one function that reuses the closeout's exact predicate and verifiers, so the two cannot diverge (R1); D1 drops expiry on the sealed path because the sealed verifier never checked it (R2). No structural fact ids were listed for mapping; the sealed design assessment is structure:design-d354476c9c16ae8a.
Examined the CLI error path (cli/review_run_provenance.go:76-80): failures still render 'pose review run proof: <reason>' with exit 1; the manual explains when the sealed versus live answer applies.

An 18-line dispatcher reusing existing verifiers, plus three one-line call-site swaps, is the smallest sufficient change; the alternative of inlining the predicate at each caller would duplicate it. No speculative extension. The choice would be invalidated if any caller used the reading answer to back a new attestation (D1 falsifier); none does today.

findings.rationale: The manual (also scaffold/dist/POSE.md:1050 and both pt-BR copies) says 'pose review run-proof and the other readers of a run's verdict' ask the sealed question, but the adjudication/smoke readers (verifiedVerdictProof via SpecAdjudications/SmokeResults -> verifiedVerdictRun) still ask the live question. As a result, the change at delegated_verdicts.go:345 has no visible effect for a drifted done scope. The gap is in the spec but not in the manual.
